Even after the recent slide, bitcoin remains up approximately 22 percent over the past month, reflecting a sharp rally through much of August that has only partially unwound in the days since. Open interest in bitcoin derivatives has climbed alongside the price swings, reaching roughly $53 billion, up about 14 percent over the past month, a sign that leveraged positioning has increased even as spot prices have softened.

content.heading: Key levels traders are watching
paragraphs: Technical analysts have identified a trading range between roughly $77,500 and $82,200 as the key band to watch in the near term. A daily close below the lower end of that range could open the door to a deeper pullback toward $75,000, while a confirmed breakout above resistance in the $82,000 to $83,200 area could set up a move toward $85,000 and eventually the $88,000 to $90,000 zone, according to chart-based analysis circulating among crypto traders.

With this week's producer and consumer price reports due before the Fed's meeting, crypto markets are likely to remain sensitive to incoming inflation data in the days ahead, alongside any further developments in the Middle East conflict that has already begun rippling through energy, precious metals and digital asset markets alike.

title: Mortgage Rates Tick Up as Oil Prices Climb
dek: The 30-year mortgage rate hovered near 6.7% as rising Treasury yields, driven partly by oil prices near $100 a barrel, kept borrowing costs elevated.
takeaways: The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate sat near 6.67% to 6.74% this week, with the 10-year Treasury yield climbing toward 4.78% as oil prices approached $100 a barrel.
The Mortgage Bankers Association and Fannie Mae both expect 30-year rates to hover between roughly 6.6% and 6.8% through the rest of 2026.
Rates are still down more than half a point since late May, helping drive a more than 62% year-over-year jump in refinance applications.

content.heading: Rates hold in a stubborn range
paragraphs: Mortgage rates remained stuck in a narrow but elevated band this week, with the average 30-year fixed rate hovering between about 6.67 percent and 6.74 percent depending on the data source, as the market absorbed a mix of holiday-thinned trading and fresh inflationary pressure from surging oil prices. The 15-year fixed rate sat in a similar pattern, ranging from roughly 6.01 percent to 6.11 percent across different daily surveys.

Rate movements have been modest day to day but meaningful over a longer horizon: the 30-year benchmark is running roughly half a percentage point higher than a year ago, even after a partial retreat from the one-year high touched in late August, when the rate briefly topped 6.78 percent following a stronger-than-expected jobs report.

content.heading: Oil prices feed through to Treasury yields
paragraphs: Much of the upward pressure on mortgage pricing this week traces back to the bond market rather than housing-specific factors. Mortgage rates don't move in lockstep with the Fed's benchmark rate; instead, they tend to track the 10-year US Treasury yield, which climbed toward 4.78 percent as oil prices pushed toward the $100-a-barrel mark amid escalating conflict between the United States and Iran. Rising energy costs feed directly into inflation expectations, which in turn push Treasury yields, and by extension mortgage rates, higher.

That transmission mechanism means mortgage borrowers have effectively been paying a price for geopolitical instability thousands of miles away, even though the immediate cause of this week's oil price spike, strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure and retaliatory US action against Iranian tankers, has nothing directly to do with US housing markets.

content.heading: Refinancing activity picks up regardless
paragraphs: Despite rates remaining well above the three to four percent levels borrowers grew accustomed to earlier in the decade, refinance activity has picked up meaningfully compared with a year ago. Rates are down more than half a percentage point since the end of May, a decline that has been enough to spark a more than 62 percent year-over-year increase in refinance applications, according to industry data cited by mortgage analysts.

For homeowners who locked in rates at the market's recent peak, even a modest half-point decline can translate into meaningful monthly savings, which analysts say helps explain the surge in refinancing interest even as the broader rate environment remains far from historically cheap.

content.heading: Forecasters see little relief through 2027
paragraphs: Looking further out, major housing finance forecasters are not projecting significant relief anytime soon. The Mortgage Bankers Association expects the 30-year rate to range between 6.60 percent and 6.70 percent through the remainder of 2026, with a similar 6.70 percent forecast carrying into 2027. Fannie Mae's outlook is slightly more cautious, projecting an average rate between 6.70 percent and 6.80 percent for both the rest of this year and into next.

With the Federal Reserve's target range still at 3.50 to 3.75 percent and a rate decision looming later this month, mortgage analysts say the coming weeks, particularly this week's producer and consumer price reports, will be pivotal in determining whether rates drift further upward or find room to ease as markets get a clearer read on the inflation outlook.

title: US Jobs Report Fuels Bets on a Fed Rate Hike
dek: August payrolls grew far faster than expected, tripling forecasts and hardening market bets that the Federal Reserve will raise rates this month.
takeaways: US nonfarm payrolls grew by 162,000 in August, roughly three times the 53,000 economists had forecast, while unemployment held steady at 4.1%.
Upward revisions to June and July payroll figures added further evidence of labor market strength heading into the Fed's September meeting.
Stocks fell on the news as investors weighed the stronger data against the increased likelihood of a Fed rate hike this month.

content.heading: Payrolls blow past expectations
paragraphs: The US labor market delivered a far stronger reading than economists had anticipated in its latest monthly snapshot, with nonfarm payrolls growing by 162,000 in August, more than triple the 53,000 jobs that had been forecast in a Dow Jones survey of economists. The unemployment rate held steady at 4.1 percent, matching expectations and underscoring a labor market that has continued to add jobs at a healthy clip even amid elevated interest rates and mounting trade tensions.

Adding to the report's strength, the Bureau of Labor Statistics revised figures for both June and July higher, meaning the underlying trend in job growth over the summer was stronger than initially reported. The combination of a large August beat and positive revisions left little room for economists to dismiss the report as a one-off anomaly.

content.heading: Markets react with a rate-hike repricing
paragraphs: Financial markets moved quickly to reprice the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike following the report's release. Futures markets shifted to reflect a substantially higher probability that the Fed's policy committee would raise its benchmark rate at the September meeting, a marked change from earlier expectations that the central bank might hold steady or even begin easing policy given ongoing concerns about the impact of tariffs on economic growth.

Major stock indexes fell in the immediate aftermath of the report, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite all posting losses as investors weighed the implications of a hotter labor market against the increased likelihood that borrowing costs would rise rather than fall in the near term.

content.heading: A complicated signal for the Fed
paragraphs: The strong jobs data arrives at a delicate moment for the Federal Reserve, which must weigh evidence of a resilient labor market against signs of persistent inflation, some of it stemming from tariffs and, more recently, from oil prices pushed higher by conflict in the Middle East. A robust labor market typically gives the central bank more room to raise rates without triggering a sharp rise in unemployment, strengthening the case made by the three FOMC members who already dissented in favor of a hike at the July meeting.

At the same time, the report complicates the political pressure campaign from the White House, which has pushed the Fed to cut rates in recent weeks. A labor market growing well above trend gives Fed officials a data-driven rationale for resisting that pressure, since a primary justification for rate cuts, a cooling job market, appears considerably weaker than it did just a month earlier.

content.heading: What comes next
paragraphs: With the jobs report now in hand, attention turns to this week's inflation data, including producer and consumer price reports covering August, as the final major inputs before the Fed's September 15-16 meeting. Economists say a hot inflation reading combined with August's strong payroll growth would make a rate hike considerably more likely, while a cooler-than-expected inflation print could reopen the door to a hold.

For now, markets are treating the jobs report as a significant data point tilting the balance toward tighter policy, with bond yields, mortgage rates and risk assets across the board already adjusting to the shifting odds in the days since the report's release.

title: NFL 2026 Season Kicks Off With Super Bowl Rematch
dek: The Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl LX rematch as the 2026 NFL season opens, with a championship banner unveiling before kickoff.
takeaways: The Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on Wednesday night in the 2026 NFL Kickoff Game, a rematch of Super Bowl LX, which Seattle won 29-13.
It marks just the third Week 1 Super Bowl rematch in NFL history and the first NFL Kickoff Game rematch in a decade.
Seattle will unveil its championship banner before kickoff, with cornerback Christian Gonzalez's new four-year, $135 million extension a major storyline entering the game.

content.heading: A rematch to open the season
paragraphs: The 2026 NFL season officially begins Wednesday night with a matchup that feels more like a playoff rematch than a Week 1 opener. The Seattle Seahawks, fresh off their Super Bowl LX title, host the New England Patriots at Lumen Field in the league's official Kickoff Game, seven months after the two teams met in the championship game in Santa Clara. Seattle won that meeting 29-13, and Wednesday's rematch marks just the third time in NFL history that the two Super Bowl participants have met again in the following season's opener.

The occasion carries extra pageantry: before kickoff, the Seahawks will unveil their championship banner, a ceremony that will play out in front of a Patriots team looking to show its rapid turnaround from last season was no fluke. New England finished 14-3 in coach Mike Vrabel's first year at the helm, an improvement tied for the largest single-season turnaround in league history after going 4-13 the year before.

content.heading: Key matchups to watch
paragraphs: Among the most anticipated individual battles is the matchup between Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the reigning Offensive Player of the Year, and New England cornerback Christian Gonzalez. The showdown gained extra significance this week when Gonzalez agreed to a four-year, $135 million contract extension, a deal that resolved a months-long dispute and had left questions about whether the Pro Bowl corner would even suit up for the opener.

Both rosters have shifted since the Super Bowl. New England added marquee free agent A.J. Brown to bolster its receiving corps around quarterback Drake Maye, while Seattle will be without Super Bowl LX MVP running back Kenneth Walker III, who departed for Kansas City in free agency during the offseason.

content.heading: Historical weight behind the rematch
paragraphs: Wednesday's game is only the twelfth regular-season meeting between teams that faced off in the previous season's Super Bowl, according to NFL research, and history has favored the reigning champion in that spot: the defending Super Bowl winner has gone 8-3 in the previous eleven such rematches. Seattle will look to add to that trend on home turf, where the Seahawks' defense and running game dominated the teams' last meeting.

The broadcast carries significance for NBC as well, marking the network's twenty-first consecutive NFL season opener and the official launch of its twenty-first season of Sunday Night Football coverage, with play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico and analyst Cris Collinsworth calling the action.

content.heading: Setting the tone for the season
paragraphs: Beyond the immediate result, Wednesday's game is expected to set an early tone for both franchises' 2026 campaigns. A Patriots win would offer an emphatic statement that New England's turnaround under Vrabel is sustainable at the highest level, while a Seahawks victory would reinforce Seattle's status as the team to beat in the NFC heading into a title defense.

With the rest of the league's Week 1 slate following over the coming days, Wednesday night's Kickoff Game gives fans their first look at how both Super Bowl LX participants have evolved since February, and an early signal of how the rest of the season's contenders might need to adjust to keep pace with the league's two most recent finalists.

title: Tiafoe Completes Epic Comeback at US Open
dek: Frances Tiafoe rallied from two sets down to beat Alex Michelsen in a five-set thriller, reaching his third US Open semifinal in five years.
takeaways: Frances Tiafoe defeated unseeded Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6(6) after trailing two sets to none, marking the first men's US Open quarterfinal comeback from two sets down since Roger Federer in 2014.
Tiafoe reached his third US Open semifinal in five years and will face the winner of Carlos Alcaraz vs. Ben Shelton.
In the women's draw, Qinwen Zheng pulled off her second straight epic comeback, rallying from 0-5 down to beat former champion Iga Swiatek and reach the quarterfinals.

content.heading: A five-set thriller for the ages
paragraphs: Frances Tiafoe produced the biggest comeback of his career on Tuesday night at Arthur Ashe Stadium, rallying from two sets down to defeat fellow American Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6) in an all-American US Open quarterfinal. The victory sends Tiafoe into his third US Open semifinal in five years, where he'll face the winner of a late match between second seed Carlos Alcaraz and eighth-seeded American Ben Shelton.

The win carried historical weight: it marked the first time since 2014, when Roger Federer came back from two sets down against Gael Monfils, that a men's US Open quarterfinal had been decided by such a comeback. Only three other such rallies have occurred at Flushing Meadows during the Open era, underscoring just how rare Tuesday's turnaround was.

content.heading: A slow start turns into a statement finish
paragraphs: Tiafoe struggled badly through the opening stretch of the match, producing a first-serve percentage below forty percent across the first three sets while Michelsen, the tournament's only remaining man not to have dropped a set, used his own serve to cruise to a two-set lead. Michelsen appeared well on his way to a first career Grand Slam semifinal after breaking early in the third set to push his advantage to 5-3.

But Tiafoe, who entered the match with a 2-17 career record at majors when trailing two sets to none, found another gear. He clawed back to win the third set 7-5, handing Michelsen his first set loss of the tournament, before taking the fourth set and grinding out a tense final-set tiebreak to complete the reversal, sending the Ashe Stadium crowd, chanting 'One, two, three, FOE' throughout, into a frenzy.

content.heading: Zheng's own miracle run
paragraphs: Tiafoe's comeback came a day after another stunning turnaround on the same court, as China's Qinwen Zheng produced her second consecutive epic rally to reach the women's quarterfinals. Trailing 0-5 in the opening set against two-time major champion Iga Swiatek, Zheng won seven straight games to steal the set before closing out a 7-5, 6-3 victory that left a shocked Swiatek in tears as she left the court.

It was the second such comeback for Zheng in as many rounds, having also rallied from 0-5 down in a deciding set to beat Madison Keys days earlier. The result advanced Zheng to a US Open quarterfinal for the third time in her career, though she has never previously progressed past that stage.

content.heading: What's next in New York
paragraphs: With the men's semifinal picture nearly set, attention now turns to whether Tiafoe can carry his momentum into a potential first career Grand Slam final appearance. On the women's side, Zheng's continued run adds another compelling storyline to a tournament that has already delivered a string of dramatic upsets and comebacks through the quarterfinal stage.

The marathon nature of several of this year's matches, including a fourth-round contest that broke the record for most points played in US Open history, has added to the sense that the 2026 tournament is shaping up as one of the more physically grueling and unpredictable editions in recent memory heading into the final rounds.

title: Mbappe Fires Real Madrid Past Inter Milan
dek: Kylian Mbappe scored his fifth goal of the season as Real Madrid held off a late Inter Milan rally to win 2-1 in their Champions League opener at the Bernabeu.
takeaways: Real Madrid beat Inter Milan 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabeu in their Champions League league-phase opener, with Kylian Mbappe and Federico Valverde scoring first-half goals.
Mbappe's strike moved him level with club legend Raul on 71 Champions League goals, making him the competition's fifth-highest all-time scorer.
Inter substitute Carlos Augusto pulled a goal back late, and Jose Mourinho earned a win against one of his former clubs, whom he led to Champions League glory in 2010.

content.heading: A nervy win to open the campaign
paragraphs: Real Madrid began their 2026-27 Champions League campaign with a hard-fought 2-1 win over Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu, a result that offered an immediate response after Friday's shock 1-0 defeat at Real Betis in La Liga. Kylian Mbappe opened the scoring in the fourteenth minute, converting after Inter goalkeeper hesitated inside his own box, before Federico Valverde doubled Madrid's lead shortly after by pouncing on the resulting loose ball.

Mbappe's goal carried historical significance beyond the three points: it moved the French forward level with Real Madrid great Raul on 71 Champions League goals, making him outright the competition's fifth-highest all-time scorer. It was Mbappe's fifth goal of the season across all competitions.

content.heading: Inter push back but fall short
paragraphs: Despite falling behind early, Inter Milan were far from passive, forcing goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois into saves from both Marcus Thuram and Lautaro Martinez before conceding, and later hitting the crossbar through Curtis Jones just before halftime. After the break, Inter continued to create chances, with Thuram again proving the visitors' most dangerous threat, before substitute Carlos Augusto finally broke through, converting a Lautaro Martinez cutback to halve the deficit and set up a tense finish.

Statistically, the underlying numbers told a complicated story: Madrid finished with the superior expected-goals tally of 2.91 to Inter's 1.78, though much of that gap stemmed from opportunities Inter effectively gifted the hosts in the first half rather than clear-cut Madrid dominance throughout.

content.heading: A meaningful night for Mourinho
paragraphs: The result carried added significance for Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho, who guided Inter to Champions League glory in 2010 and faced his former club for the first time since taking over in Madrid. Opposing manager Cristian Chivu was himself part of that title-winning Inter squad from sixteen years earlier, adding a layer of shared history to the encounter at the same stadium where Mourinho's Inter side beat Bayern Munich in that 2010 final.

Mourinho made two changes to his starting lineup for the match, bringing in Trent Alexander-Arnold and Brahim Diaz in place of the suspended pairing of Eduardo Camavinga and Arda Guler, adjustments that factored into a first half in which Madrid capitalized on Inter's uncharacteristic defensive lapses.

content.heading: Work still to do, Mourinho admits
paragraphs: Despite the win, observers were quick to note that Madrid were fortunate to come away with all three points given how the underlying performance played out, a sign, according to analysts covering the match, that there remains significant work ahead if Mourinho's side hopes to mount a serious Champions League title challenge this season.

The victory nonetheless gives Real Madrid a winning start to the newly formatted league phase, while Inter will look to bounce back in their next continental fixture as both sides continue balancing European ambitions with their respective domestic campaigns in LaLiga and Serie A.

title: Solheim Cup Tees Off With Europe Seeking Revenge
dek: The 2026 Solheim Cup begins Friday at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, with Europe looking to reclaim the trophy on home soil behind stars Charley Hull and Lottie Woad.
takeaways: The 20th Solheim Cup begins Friday at Bernardus Golf in Cromvoirt, Netherlands, with Europe, captained by Anna Nordqvist, hosting the United States, captained by Angela Stanford.
Team USA won the 2024 edition 15.5-12.5 in Virginia, its first Solheim Cup win since 2017, and now holds an 11-8 advantage in the biennial series.
The last three Solheim Cups held in Europe have produced the closest finishes in the event's history, including the first-ever 14-14 tie in 2023.

content.heading: Europe hosts with revenge on its mind
paragraphs: The 2026 Solheim Cup gets underway Friday at Bernardus Golf in Cromvoirt, Netherlands, with Europe looking to reclaim the trophy on home soil two years after suffering a 15.5-12.5 defeat to the United States in Virginia. That result snapped a run of European dominance and handed the Americans their first win in the biennial contest since 2017, leaving captain Anna Nordqvist's side with a clear mission heading into this year's edition.

The three-day event runs through Sunday, with the opening two days featuring foursomes and four-ball match play before Sunday's decisive singles session, mirroring the format familiar to fans of the men's Ryder Cup. Twelve players from each side will compete across a maximum of twenty-eight points, with 14.5 points needed to win the cup outright.

content.heading: Star power on both sides
paragraphs: England's Charley Hull headlines Team Europe as one of the competition's most experienced stalwarts, having already claimed a Ladies European Tour title this year at the PIF Saudi Ladies International. She'll be joined by Lottie Woad, who turned professional a little over a year ago and has already climbed into the world's top ten, making her Solheim Cup debut alongside fellow rookies among Nordqvist's captain's picks.

For the Americans, Nelly Korda enters as the marquee name after a stretch of dominant form that saw her win four LPGA Tour events and finish no worse than eighth across a ten-tournament run earlier this season, along with a successful title defense at the US Women's Open. Angela Stanford, taking charge of her first US Solheim Cup team after three stints as an assistant captain, will lean heavily on that form as she looks to extend America's current era of success in the event.

content.heading: A history of nail-biters in Europe
paragraphs: History suggests this year's edition could once again go down to the wire. The last three Solheim Cups staged on European soil have produced the three closest finishes in the competition's twenty-edition history, with both the 2015 and 2019 contests decided by a single point and the 2023 edition at Finca Cortesin in Spain producing the first 14-14 tie ever recorded in the event.

Of the nine previous editions held in Europe, the home side has won five and lost three, giving Nordqvist's team a modest historical edge in front of what is expected to be a passionate crowd at Bernardus, a Kyle Phillips-designed course making its Solheim Cup debut this week.

content.heading: Setting the stage for Sunday
paragraphs: The tournament follows the conclusion of Tuesday's Ping Junior Solheim Cup, also contested at Bernardus for the first time in the junior event's history, which Team USA won 13-11 after holding off a furious late rally from their European counterparts. Several past junior competitors, including Rose Zhang and Nelly Korda herself, have gone on to represent their countries in the senior event, underscoring the pipeline between the two competitions.

With qualifying now complete and both twelve-player rosters set, attention turns fully to Friday's opening foursomes session, where fans on both sides of the Atlantic will be watching closely to see whether Europe can deliver the bounce-back performance it has been chasing since its defeat two years ago.

title: Ryan Garcia Defends Title Against Conor Benn
dek: Ryan Garcia makes the first defense of his WBC welterweight title against Conor Benn on September 12 in Las Vegas, headlining a stacked Mexican Independence Day card.
takeaways: Ryan Garcia defends his WBC welterweight title against Conor Benn on Saturday, September 12, at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, streaming live on Paramount+.
The fight fills the Mexican Independence Day weekend slot originally reserved for Canelo Alvarez's title challenge against Christian Mbilli, which was postponed to late October.
Benn, son of former champion Nigel Benn, is fighting for his first world title after avenging his loss to Chris Eubank Jr. and beating former champion Regis Prograis.

content.heading: A title fight fills a marquee weekend
paragraphs: Ryan Garcia will make the first defense of his WBC welterweight championship against Britain's Conor Benn on Saturday, September 12, at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, a matchup that has taken on added significance after stepping into the Mexican Independence Day weekend slot long associated with Canelo Alvarez. Alvarez's own title challenge against Christian Mbilli, originally scheduled for the same date and venue, was postponed to late October, opening the door for Garcia and Benn to headline boxing's biggest weekend of the year instead.

Garcia, twenty-seven, captured the WBC belt in February with a dominant unanimous decision over Mario Barrios at the same T-Mobile Arena, a win that offered stability after a turbulent few years in and out of the ring. Saturday's fight returns him to the venue where he won the title for his first defense of the championship.

content.heading: Benn chasing history in the US
paragraphs: For Conor Benn, the fight represents a chance to accomplish something his father, former middleweight and super-middleweight champion Nigel Benn, achieved decades earlier: winning a world title on American soil. The twenty-nine-year-old earned his shot after avenging his lone professional loss to Chris Eubank Jr. and following that up with a win over former world champion Regis Prograis on the undercard of Tyson Fury's comeback bout in April.

Benn enters the bout with a 26-1 professional record, and promoters have framed the matchup as a genuine clash of styles, pitting Garcia's power and boxing ability against Benn's activity and pressure, with betting markets making Garcia a significant favorite at odds of -370 to Benn's +275.

content.heading: A stacked undercard
paragraphs: The main event is supported by a deep undercard featuring several title fights of its own. In the co-main event, unbeaten cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia defends his Zuffa Boxing and Ring Magazine titles against Noel Mikaelyan, while other bouts on the nine-fight card include lightweight Mark Magsayo facing Andres Cortes and welterweights Jose Ramirez and Alexis Rocha squaring off in a separate matchup.

The event streams exclusively on Paramount+ in the United States at no additional cost beyond a standard subscription, a notable departure from the pay-per-view model that has traditionally accompanied cards of this magnitude, with the promotion emphasizing broad accessibility for what is expected to be one of the year's most-watched boxing events.

content.heading: What a win would mean
paragraphs: A victory for Garcia would cement his position as one of the sport's biggest active stars and validate his rapid ascent back to championship level after a career marked by both dazzling performances and personal setbacks. For Benn, an upset win would rank among the biggest results in recent British boxing history and would immediately establish him as a mainstream force in the stacked welterweight division.

With Alvarez's own return now pushed to late October, Saturday's Garcia-Benn card effectively inherits the mantle of the sport's marquee Mexican Independence Day weekend event, giving both men a rare opportunity to headline boxing's biggest annual showcase in the champion's absence.
